item.description: - Opening at login is honest about itself now. The switch reads whether macOS has actually registered Intention rather than what it was last told, so turning Intention off in System Settings is reflected here instead of the switch going on claiming it's on. - If macOS is holding the login item pending your approval — which it does sometimes, and which the app can't clear on its own — Intention says so and offers to open the right pane of System Settings, rather than appearing to be on while never starting. - Running Intention straight from the disk image or your Downloads folder now explains why opening at login and automatic updates can't work from there, instead of both quietly failing. Dragging it to Applications fixes both, and that's what it tells you.

- Intention no longer offers you an update while it's asking what you intend to do. The update window would have opened behind the overlay, which holds the screen and keeps taking focus back — leaving you unable to answer the question or dismiss the update. A check that arrives at a bad moment now waits for the overlay to close rather than being dropped.
